clue.text: Stress in the tube?

definitions.meaning: to stress a word in writing is to draw a rule beneath it
read as ..., a train on a line of the London Underground, nicknamed the Tube

explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the everyday name for the London Underground, whose routes are called lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing a rule beneath words is a way of giving them emphasis, the written equivalent of stress.

clue.text: Decree to take Britain as English

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for Britain

explanation.surface: A ruling that obliges Britain to be counted as English.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was an edict of the Russian tsar, and loosely any arbitrary order or decree.

clue.text: Take away from foreign land

parts.note: de is the French (a foreign language) word for from
a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: Someone removing something from a land abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to diminish or subtract something, especially from merit or value.

clue.text: Note girl gets to bailiff

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl comes to a bailiff about a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a manorial steward or local magistrate in medieval England, a bailiff's role.

clue.text: Plant setter's getting for the time being

parts.note: to plant can mean to bury, which is to inter
the setter is I, so setter's is I'm (I am)

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker acquiring a plant only temporarily.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is provisional, lasting only until something permanent replaces it.

clue.text: Lively Frenchman backed to become in charge

indicators.note: backed means the Frenchman's name is written from back to front

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name
to get, as in get angry, means to become

explanation.surface: A vigorous Frenchman who backs a bid to take control.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic means full of vigour and activity, a synonym of lively.

clue.text: She combines with it to be poetic

definitions.text: She combines with it to be poetic

indicators.note: combines tells us to mix the letters of this word with those of it to make a word meaning poetic

parts.note: taken as written: its letters are the pool
taken as written: its letters are added to the answer

explanation.surface: A woman who joins with something to become lyrical.
explanation.walkthrough: Add IT to the answer and rearrange the six letters to spell POETIC; 'She' just stands for the answer, a word that 'combines' with IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is identified purely by the letter play: four letters which, mixed with two others, form the given word.

clue.text: Watertight chamber is thus in metal shell

indicators.note: in puts is and thus inside the tin can

parts.note: a can is a metal container, a shell of tin
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A sealed compartment sits thus within an armoured casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A caisson is a watertight structure in which people work underwater, as on bridge foundations.

clue.text: 8 in itself quaintly pleasing

definitions.note: the answer to 8 across, meaning to treat cruelly

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself
cute means attractive in a quaint or endearing way

explanation.surface: Something cruel that is also, in itself, oddly charming.
explanation.definitionFit: To persecute is to harass and ill-treat someone persistently, to maltreat them.

clue.text: Scotch perhaps about a time to bully

parts.note: a malt is a whisky, Scotch for example
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Whisky makes someone take a moment to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat is to treat badly or cruelly, which is what a bully does.

clue.text: Recorder backing work for asylum seeker?

parts.note: EMI is a famous record company, a recorder of music

indicators.note: backing means the word for work is set down back to front

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A recording artist supporting a piece of work for a refugee.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigre is someone who has left their country, often for political reasons, as a refugee might.

clue.text: One that makes master feel inadequate?

definitions.text: One that makes master feel inadequate?

indicators.note: inadequate suggests the letters are not right as they stand and need reworking

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Someone who leaves a man in charge feeling not up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' mixes MA and FEEL; and the whole clue hints that a woman can make her lord and master feel lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman, the opposite sex to a master, is cast as one who leaves him feeling inferior.

clue.text: Boy tries out record

parts.note: Reg is a boy's name, short for Reginald

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A lad has a go at some records.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is an official list or record, as of births or of pupils.

clue.text: Chuffed by story about party leader

indicators.note: about means the story is turned round, back to front

parts.note: a tale is a story
Ed Miliband led the Labour Party when this was set

explanation.surface: Someone pleased by a tale concerning the head of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TALE into ELAT. 'Chuffed' is British slang for delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean delighted or in high spirits.

clue.text: Crete lies roughly somewhere between Reykjavik and Aden!

indicators.note: roughly means the letters are given only approximately, rearranged

explanation.surface: An island said to be roughly between Iceland and Yemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges CRETE LIES. Leicester, an English city, does sit vaguely on a line between the Icelandic and Yemeni capitals; Crete does not.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a playfully vague location that a city in the English Midlands technically satisfies.

clue.text: Politicians find rising star come to dead end

indicators.note: in a down light rising means everything after it is read from bottom to top
end means the final letter of dead

explanation.surface: A star rises and then meets a dead end, as politicians do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the whole run STAR + COME + D (the 'end' of 'dead').
explanation.definitionFit: Democrats are members of a political party, notably in the US, so politicians.

clue.text: Revolting classic character can love America

parts.note: mu is a letter of the classical Greek alphabet
a tin is a can
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
US is the United States, America

explanation.surface: A disgusting old character who can love the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolting here means rising in revolt, which is what the mutinous do.

clue.text: Spice for 15 Roman character early in the week

parts.note: Cinna is a conspirator in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, a mutinous Roman
Mon, Monday, comes early in the week

explanation.surface: A seasoning fit for a rebellious Roman at the start of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is MUTINOUS; Cinna plotted against Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon is a common spice from the bark of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Like marriage taking up Latin translation

indicators.note: translation turns the words into a new form, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Wedding vows taken up in a Latin version.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial means relating to a wedding or marriage.

clue.text: One sea and other river nymphs

indicators.note: other suggests a different arrangement of the letters

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sea creature and a few other water spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads, plural naiades, are the water nymphs of rivers and springs in Greek myth.

clue.text: Slight arch on East Sussex shore?

definitions.meaning: a gentle convex curve, as on a road surface
... is a coastal village in East Sussex, a county in southern England, famous for ... Sands

explanation.definitionFit: A road's convex curve is its camber, and Camber is also a seaside place in southern England.

clue.text: A bit in France sounds a fortiori here

indicators.note: sounds tells us the answer is said like the phrase meaning a fortiori

parts.note: a fortiori is Latin for with greater reason, more so

explanation.surface: A Latin term for a stronger argument has a French ring to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Morceau is French for a piece or bit, also used of a short musical piece.

clue.text: His name gained New World prominence

definitions.text: His name gained New World prominence

parts.words: His name gained New World prominence
parts.note: Amerigo, the explorer's first name, became America, the name of the New World

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian navigator Amerigo Vespucci gave his forename, in Latin form, to the Americas.

clue.text: Element slightly indecent in church office

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol of copper, an element
racy means a little risque

explanation.surface: Something a touch risque found in an ecclesiastical department.
explanation.definitionFit: A curacy is the post or benefice of a curate, an office in the church.

clue.text: Hunt with no time to be modest

indicators.note: with no means the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: chaste means modest, pure

explanation.surface: A pursuit with no time left for decorum.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase is to pursue or hunt.

clue.text: Belief being firm about colour

indicators.note: about places the firm's letters around the colour

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A conviction that a company sticks to its colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a statement of belief.

clue.text: Conqueror turned to race, inter alia

indicators.note: turned means the result is read backwards
inter is Latin for between, so the race goes in among the letters

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorbike race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A warrior turned to racing, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alia' looks like the Latin phrase for among other things, but 'inter' (between) works as a container signal on ALIA; 'turned' then reverses ALITTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila the Hun conquered much of central and eastern Europe in the fifth century.

clue.text: Time read out from one side to the other

definitions.text: from one side to the other

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A clock reading given from end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is a line crossing a circle through its centre, from side to side.

clue.text: What's said or sung, but not at church

indicators.note: but not at means the church abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: choral means sung by a choir

explanation.surface: Speech or song, only not in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written.

clue.text: Number turn out after emergency call and keep it going

indicators.note: after puts the number and the shuffled word behind the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
ten is a number

indicators.note: turn means the word out is turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A number appears after a distress call, telling responders to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: Sostenuto is a musical direction to sustain the notes, keeping each sound going.
